traits.use — agent & contributor guide

Source: AGENTS.md

traits.use is an R package for loading, exploring and wrangling data from any traits.build relational trait database, such as AusTraits. It began as the austraits package and was split out in 2026 (traitecoevo/austraits#188, history carried over). austraits (4.0.0) is now a thin AusTraits-specific layer over it. 0.1.1 (2026-11-23) was a GitHub-only release. 1.0.0 (2026-11-24, maintainer Elizabeth Wenk), the release for AusTraits 8.0.0, is released on GitHub (#17); its CRAN submission is tracked in #13.

Repo-local guidance

  • Code: R/ (functions), tests/ (testthat), man/ (generated docs), NAMESPACE, data-raw/ and inst/ hold raw assets (incl. the cheatsheet); data/austraits_lite.rda is the exported example database (24 datasets, used by the examples), regenerated with data-raw/austraits_lite.R; austraits_lite is also the tests’ main fixture. R/sysdata.rda holds austraits_5.0.0_lite (9 datasets of AusTraits 5.0.0, regenerated with data-raw/austraits_5.0.0_lite.R), for the tests of releases built before traits.build 2.3: no data model version, the old reference columns of methods, sources a plain BibEntry. Releases before 5.0.0 are not supported (decided 2026-11-25) and have no fixture. Write new tests against austraits_lite; use the 5.0.0 fixture only for what is specific to the older form.
  • austraits_lite follows the data model, not the AusTraits releases (decided 2026-11-24, #13). It is compiled from austraits.build source at a pinned commit, because traits.use must be released before the AusTraits release whose data model it reads. Rebuild it whenever traits.build changes the data model; test-data.R fails where traits.build is installed until you do. Release order: traits.build develop → rebuild austraits_lite → traits.use release → traits.build release → AusTraits release. Update ?austraits_lite (R/data.R) and inst/COPYRIGHTS with the commit.
  • Hex and cheat sheet (decided 2026-11-25): the hex, man/figures/logo.png, is drawn by data-raw/hex.R (traits.build’s look, with the AusTraits sprig, data-raw/austraits_sprig.svg, stamped on the database). The cheat sheet’s source is inst/cheatsheet/traits.use-cheatsheet.pptx; after editing it, export the PDF beside it and man/figures/traits.use-cheatsheet.png (the README’s image, e.g. pdftoppm -png -r 100 -singlefile). It is set in Source Sans Pro and Menlo: a LibreOffice export needs both in the profile’s user/fonts folder, or it substitutes a serif. Update it when exported functions or their arguments change.
  • Access entry point: load_database() (R/load_database.R) loads any traits.build database from its doi (Zenodo, Figshare, or a doi resolving directly to an .rds). flattened = TRUE loads the flattened table and means = TRUE the observed means published with the release (*-observed-means.csv.gz); means_file() picks that file and cached_records() (R/database_cache.R) must know every kind of file load_database() downloads. list_versions() (R/list_versions.R) lists a record’s releases; it resolves a doi with the same helpers as load_database(), at the end of R/load_database.R.
  • AusTraits-specific code lives in austraits, not here (decided 2026-11-14, #13): load_austraits(), get_versions() / get_version_latest(), the AusTraits vignette and the map of Australia. The generic part of get_versions() is list_versions() here (#52), which lists the releases of any Zenodo or Figshare record. plot_locations() draws over a world map cropped to the locations by default (inst/extdata/world_land.rds, from data-raw/world_land.R), and takes a basemap data frame so austraits can pass its map.
  • Wrangle/extract: extract_*() (data/dataset/taxa/trait), join_*() (taxa, methods, contributors, locations, context/location properties), lookup_*(), trait_pivot_longer/wider(), summarise_database(), bind_databases(), flatten_database(), as_wide_table().
  • Trait means: summarise_trait_means() (R/summarise_trait_means.R, #50) gives one row per taxon and trait: the observed mean of a numeric trait (a geometric mean) and the most frequent value of a categorical one, optionally split by further variables. It takes both input formats. AusTraits publishes its output with each release (austraits.build’s post_export()), and the API and portal are to read that file, so a change to the method changes published numbers: say so in NEWS. The method’s terms (“observed mean”, never “average”) follow terminology.md in traitecoevo/austraits-means. It is computed with group indices and rowsum(), not a grouped summarise(), which is about a hundred times slower on a full database (3.5 s against 100 s on AusTraits); keep it that way.
  • Two input formats, told apart by class (#41): the relational database (list, class traits.build) and a flat table (data frame; flatten_database() output has class traits.build_flat and a traits.build_stamp attribute). database_format() in R/check_compatibility.R is the one place that decides; don’t branch on dim() or is_tibble(). extract_trait/taxa/dataset/data(), summarise_database(), summarise_trait_means() and the plots take both, so test them with both (tests/testthat/test-flat.R); everything else stops on a flat table, via check_compatibility() or abort_flat_input().
  • Build/test (standard R-package workflow): devtools::load_all(), devtools::test(), devtools::check(). The package targets R >= 4.1.0 (it uses |>); tidyverse-style Imports (dplyr, tidyr, purrr, etc.). Lifecycle badge is experimental until the first CRAN release.
  • Default branch: master. Docs/pkgdown site at https://traitecoevo.github.io/traits.use/.
  • CRAN-bound: traits.use must never Import/Depend on traits.build (not on CRAN, and +57 recursive dependencies). Keep network tests behind skip_on_cran() / skip_if_offline().

Heads-up: traits.use (like austraits before it) is the downstream access/wrangle layer in the data pipeline, but the R-package install graph runs the other way — traits.build Depends on traits.use (>= 1.0.0) and imports a few conversion helpers from it (convert_df_to_list, convert_list_to_df1, convert_list_to_df2, bind_databases, flatten_database) and re-exports the trait plots (plot_trait_distribution(), plot_categorical_trait_distribution(), plot_trait_distribution_jitter()). Changing any of these can break traits.build; run its tests after touching them. austraits and austraits.portal also Import traits.use, and austraits re-exports nearly every traits.use function (wrapping plot_locations()), so adding, renaming or removing an export here needs a matching change there.

Heads-up: from Sept 2024 the code works against any traits.build database (not just austraits.build). austraits.build versions < 5.0 are unsupported by the current package — older builds need an older tagged austraits (e.g. traitecoevo/austraits@v2.2.2).

AusTraits family — cross-package context

traits.use is part of the AusTraits family (a subset of the traitecoevo org) — here, the user-facing access/wrangle API (R package) for traits.build-format databases, including AusTraits; loads the released .rds via load_database(). Family-wide concerns are documented centrally in austraits-meta — don’t restate them here, read them there:

  • Start with AGENTS.md — pipeline order, who owns what, dependency direction, source-of-truth rules, cross-boundary artifacts, gotchas.
  • dependencies.yml — machine-readable package graph + cross-boundary artifacts.
  • governance/ — label taxonomy, board #9 conventions, release playbooks, triage.

Filing issues: the whole family is tracked on one board, AusTraits #9 (new issues auto-add to it). Follow the issue & labelling guide: pick one work-type label (bug / task / epic); Status and Priority are set on the board, not as labels.

Commit messages: every family repo squash-merges, so the PR title and body become the permanent commit message. Keep the subject ≤50 characters as typed and the body ≤10 lines; put the working detail — what you tried, benchmarks, test counts, rejected alternatives — in the first PR comment instead. Full convention: commit-messages.md.

austraits-meta is hand-maintained prose — a map, not ground truth. Verify specifics against the actual repos.
